prompt:
In MySQL, DROP INDEX concurrently ON t fails with a ParseError: concurrently should be read as the index name here. In ALTER TABLE as well, DROP INDEX concurrently must give an exp.Drop whose first table is named concurrently with its concurrently flag False, and a bare ALTER TABLE t DROP <name> (no COLUMN) must keep meaning a column drop even for keyword-like names such as temporary or iceberg. The same applies to the MySQL-family dialects Doris and StarRocks.

For example:

```python
from sqlglot import parse_one, transpile, exp

parse_one("DROP INDEX concurrently ON t", read="mysql").sql("mysql")
# currently: ParseError: Expected table name but got <Token token_type: TokenType.ON, text: ON, line: 1, col: 26, start: 24, end: 25, comments: []>. Line 1, Col: 26.
# expected:  DROP INDEX concurrently ON t
```

Other forms of the same constructs described above should work as well.

         )
+        self.validate_identity(
+            "ALTER TABLE t DROP temporary", "ALTER TABLE t DROP COLUMN temporary"
+        )
+        self.validate_identity("ALTER TABLE t DROP iceberg", "ALTER TABLE t DROP COLUMN iceberg")
         self.validate_identity("ALTER TABLE t DROP date", "ALTER TABLE t DROP COLUMN date")
         self.validate_identity(
             "ALTER TABLE t DROP concurrently", "ALTER TABLE t DROP COLUMN concurrently"
@@ -417,9 +421,14 @@ class TestMySQL(Validator):
         self.validate_identity("ALTER TABLE t DROP COLUMN concurrently").args["actions"][
             0
         ].assert_is(exp.Drop)
-        self.validate_identity("ALTER TABLE t DROP INDEX concurrently").args["actions"][
-            0

+        drop = (
